title.narrative: Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: In July 2022, Government of Zambia launched the National Action Plan (2023 – 2027) for skills anticipation, contributing towards achieving the Economic Transformation and Job Creation agenda as espoused in the Eight National Development Plan 2022-2026. The plan identifies and measures skills mismatches and anticipates future skill needs considering labour market demands in response to industrial, sectoral, trade, technology or environmental changes, including the impact of the COVID-19 crisis, using ILO tools, methodologies and approaches. The Ministry of Labour and Social Security in collaboration with key stakeholders and cooperating partners are resolved to implement the National Action Plan and contribute towards job creation and skills development in the country. In efforts to enhance skills development and Anticipation, International Labour Organization through the ILO Skills Initiative for Africa(SIFA), a programme of the African Union Commission and African Union Development Agency (AUDA-NEPAD), assisted financially by the German Government and European Union(EU) provided technical support to the Ministry of Labour and Social Security to strengthen Zambia’s Labour Market Information (LMI) and Skills Anticipation System. On March 16 2022 the ILO CO Lusaka conducted a breakfast meeting to introduce the concept of skills anticipation to the Tripartite. Present at the breakfast meeting included were the Minister of Labour and Social Security, and representatives of Workers’ and Employers’ organizations. Further, on 8th and 9th June 2022 the ILO hosted a technical meeting in Chongwe at Mika Convention Centre to draft the Skills Anticipation Plan 2023-2027 for Zambia. The ILO further reviewed the draft document and provided useful lessons from other countries which were incorporated in the final document.

Output 3.1. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement national employment policies in response to the COVID-19 crisis

description.narrative: In July 2023, the in the framework of joint programming, the ILO being part of the UN joint team on Youth initiatives, supported the Government of Zambia to developed the 2023 National Youth Policy that articulates a set of measures and provisions aimed at promoting youth employment on the demand side such as entrepreneurship development, technology and innovation measures included in the policy to promote youth development within a by 2026 defined timeframe, including in response to the COVID-19 crisis. The Policy’s employment objectives are in line with new generation National Employment Policies and the ILO’s approach and provisions of ILO Employment Policy Convention No. 122 which promotes everyone’s right to work, and represents the priorities of the new Government as espoused in their Party Manifesto and the 8NDP, which seeks to achieve economic transformation and job creation particularly for the youth. The Policy is gender responsive and thereby intends to level the playing field for the participation and inclusion of marginalised and underrepresented sections of society such as women, Youth with Disabilities and other youth categories. The Policy reflects the ILO Centenary Declaration for the Future of Work, addressing a number of country-specific future of work challenges faced by the large youth demographic and emerging issues such as mental health. The Policy has also incorporated including emerging issues such as mental health. The policy incorporates a Monitoring framework to facilitate the tracking of progress on key indicators on youth empowerment in the country. With support from RBTC funding and in the framework of joint implementation the ILO was one of the UN agencies in Zambia, supporting the Government to develop a national Youth Development Policy. In July 2023, ILO provided inputs to ensure alignment of the draft policy document with emerging trends such as pandemics, climate change, youth with disability, Just Transition and formalization of the informal sector, which employs a huge number of youths in Zambia.
